sentence: ___ (seldom / we / see) such dedication in young athletes.
explanation: La inversión con "seldom" requiere que el verbo auxiliar vaya antes del sujeto: Seldom + aux + subject + verb.
tip: Reorder the words using fronted-adverb inversion

sentence: ___ (know) about the party, I would have attended.
explanation: Condicional invertida de tercer tipo: Had + subject + past participle = If I had known.
tip: Third conditional inversion — drop 'if' and invert

sentence: ___ (not only / he / finish) the race, but he also won it.
explanation: La inversión con "not only" requiere: Not only + aux + subject + verb.
tip: Reorder using 'not only' fronted inversion

sentence: ___ (no sooner / she / arrive) than the phone rang.
explanation: La inversión con 'no sooner... than': No sooner + had + subject + past participle.
tip: Reorder using 'no sooner... than' — past perfect inversion

sentence: ___ (little / he / know) the challenges that lay ahead.
explanation: La inversión con "little": Little + aux + subject + verb.
tip: Reorder using fronted-adverb inversion

sentence: ___ (only when / the sun / set) did they decide to leave.
explanation: Con "only when", la inversión ocurre en la cláusula principal (did they decide), no en la subordinada.
tip: The inversion is already in the main clause — complete the 'only when' part

sentence: ___ (such / the impact) of the speech that everyone was moved.
explanation: Inversión con "such": Such + was/were + subject.
tip: Reorder using 'such... that' emphatic inversion

sentence: ___ (under no circumstances / you / should / open) that door.
correct: Under no circumstances should you open
explanation: Con expresiones negativas: negative expression + aux + subject + verb.
tip: Reorder the words — negative adverbial goes first, then invert subject and auxiliary

sentence: ___ (rarely / I / see) such a beautiful painting.
explanation: Inversión con "rarely": Rarely + have/has + subject + past participle.
tip: Reorder using fronted-adverb inversion — present perfect

sentence: ___ (no sooner / he / finish) his work than he went home.
explanation: La inversión con 'no sooner... than': No sooner + had + subject + past participle.
tip: Reorder using 'no sooner... than' — past perfect inversion

sentence: ___ (hardly / she / leave) when it started to rain.
explanation: La inversión con 'hardly... when': Hardly + had + subject + past participle.
tip: Reorder using 'hardly... when' — past perfect inversion

sentence: ___ (so / successful / the project) that it was expanded globally.
explanation: Inversión con 'so + adjective': So + adj + was/were + subject.
tip: Reorder using 'so... that' emphatic inversion

sentence: ___ (never before / technology / advance) so rapidly.
explanation: Inversión con "never before": Never before + has/have + subject + past participle.
tip: Reorder using fronted-adverb inversion — present perfect

sentence: ___ (on no account / you / be / to disclose) this information.
correct: On no account are you to disclose
explanation: Con "on no account": negative expression + aux + subject + verb.
tip: Reorder — negative adverbial goes first, then invert

sentence: ___ (I / win) the lottery, I would travel the world.
explanation: Condicional invertida de segundo tipo: Were + subject + to + verb = If I were to win.
tip: Second conditional inversion — drop 'if', use 'were... to'

sentence: ___ (only by / work / together / we / can / achieve) our goals.
correct: Only by working together can we achieve
explanation: Con "only by + -ing", la inversión ocurre en la cláusula principal: Only by + -ing + aux + subject + verb.
tip: Reorder — 'only by' phrase first, then invert the main clause

sentence: ___ (not until / all the guests / leave) did she finally relax.
correct: Not until all the guests had left
explanation: Con "not until", la inversión ocurre en la cláusula principal (did she relax). La subordinada usa past perfect.
tip: The inversion is already in the main clause — complete the 'not until' part with past perfect

sentence: ___ (so / quickly / he / run) that he broke the world record.
explanation: Inversión con 'so + adverb': So + adverb + aux + subject + verb.
tip: Reorder using 'so... that' emphatic inversion with an adverb

sentence: ___ (you / require) any further assistance, please do not hesitate to ask.
explanation: Condicional invertida de primer tipo: Should + subject + verb = If you require.
tip: First conditional inversion — drop 'if', use formal inverted form

sentence: ___ (in no way / he / be / responsible) for the accident.
correct: In no way is he responsible
explanation: Con "in no way": negative expression + aux + subject + complement.
tip: Reorder — negative adverbial goes first, then invert subject and 'be'
